newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudanese government says it repelled rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese government says it repelled rebel attack.

text.p: An official Sudanese newspaper said on Sunday government troops fought off a rebel attack in the east of the country, killing at least two rebels for no casualties on the government side.
The rebel force had come into Sudan from Eritrea, where the Sudanese opposition in exile has military bases, the newspaper al-Ingaz al-Watani said.
The skirmish took place last Thursday at a place called Modississa, it said. It did not say exactly where this was.
Opposition forces said on Friday they killed nine government soldiers and destroyed one vehicle in an operation in the east of the country, also last Thursday.
The Sudan Alliance Forces, military wing of the National Democratic Alliance, said they attacked the government troops 45 km (28 miles) southwest of Kassala town.
Opposition forces began attacks in eastern Sudan earlier this year, apparently from their bases in Eritrea.

The National Democratic Alliance is a broad coalition of opposition groups, including the Umma Party and the Democratic Unionists, traditionally Sudan's two biggest parties, and southern rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Army.
It advocates armed struggle to overthrow Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, who took power in 1989 in a military coup against a democratically elected government.
